_comment: Milestone 59C-1 runtime baseline. Written so 59C-2 (artifact reuse, shared parsers) and 59C-3 (observable waits) have a before-figure to claim against, and so 59C-4 has something to compare a multi-worker run to. Measured on one Windows workstation; these are not portable constants.

conditions.note: Measured AFTER 59C-0 landed. Not comparable to the 671-test figure in MILESTONE-59-PROPOSAL.md's scoping section, which was taken at e1228fd before 59A/59B.

unit.wall_note: Measured by a separate `npm run test:unit` invocation. The combined `npm test` run cannot separate it: Playwright's own 25.7m covers nearly the whole wall time.

e2e.flaky_note: Zero. The two 'retry' matches in the run log are test TITLES (offline.spec.ts 'can retry', vendor-loader-retry.spec.ts), not retry events.

artifacts.measurement_note: Lower bound, not a true peak. Sampling ran every 60s and its last sample landed 50s before the run ended, with the series still rising. Peak must be observed DURING the run: Playwright discards traces for passing tests at the end, so measuring afterward reports near-zero. Larger than the 1.38 GiB / 32,299 files quoted in the proposal's scoping section, which was itself a point-in-time observation of a different run.
artifacts.retained_by_policy: This size is a deliberate cost. 59C-1 kept trace: 'retain-on-failure' locally rather than C6's proposed 'off', because local work dominates this repo and an undiagnosable local failure costs more than disk. CI uses on-first-retry.

after_59c_and_59d._comment: Closing measurement, same workstation, taken via `npm run test:verify` at commit 7438d32 once every 59C/59D sub-delivery had landed. Recorded so the milestone's runtime claim can be checked rather than taken on trust.
after_59c_and_59d.interpretation: Consistent with C2's artifact reuse (measured at ~54s saved across four specs in isolation), not proof of it: this is a single full-run sample at each configuration, and 4.7% is close to the run-to-run variation a suite of this length can produce. Subset runs were highly repeatable (92/92/92s, 139/140/140s, 52.4/52.5s), which supports the direction. Note the total is not like-for-like with the baseline's 1544s: test:verify additionally runs check:types and verify:data-model, which npm test does not, so the e2e figure is the comparable one.
after_59c_and_59d.counts_unchanged: 678 discovered / 672 passed / 6 skipped, identical to the baseline. 59C-0 deleted an assertion, not a test; no test was added or lost anywhere in 59C or 59D.

findings_for_later_sub_deliveries.59C-3: signature-capture.contract.spec.ts is the 2nd slowest file (93.7s / 36 tests) and holds 19 of the suite's 27 waitForTimeout calls. The baseline independently confirms it as the right starting point.
findings_for_later_sub_deliveries.59C-2: The Excel export specs 59C-2 targets are well represented in the slowest tests: excel-b4-multi-account, excel-pruned-roundtrip (x2), annual-mount, guardian-inventory-mount and guardian-blank-page-pruning are 6 of the slowest 10, at 6.5-8.1s each. Those are the redundant workbook generations C2 removes.
findings_for_later_sub_deliveries.59C-4: DEFERRED, workers:1 retained. Probed cheaply instead of running the gate: four light contract specs (139 tests) went 273s serial -> 139s/140s/140s at --workers=4, three consecutive runs, zero failures and zero flakes. The config comment's claim that concurrent contexts overload the shared Vite server did NOT reproduce. Predicted ceiling from the file timings below (heavy 523s/31 files serial, light 965s/60 files parallel, 54s overhead): 17.7 min at 2 workers, 15.0 at 3, 13.6 at 4 -- the 4-worker probe landed within a point of that, so the model is sound. Still untested: the heavy specs (PDF, Excel, downloads, service-worker, cross-tab) at concurrency, which is the real risk and a ~10-minute probe.
